initial_inventory.title: [Bugfix][SM70] Serialize set-valued policy fields in the acceleration report

metadata.title: [Bugfix][SM70] Serialize set-valued policy fields in the acceleration report
metadata.body:
## Purpose

`linear_policy_report()` and the loaded-kernel report JSON-encode each resolved SM70 policy with `asdict()`. Resolved tensor-dump policies carry `frozenset` filters (layer and shape selections, for example `frozenset((0, 1))` for the `qwen_layer` channel), and `json.dumps` raises:

```
TypeError: Object of type frozenset is not JSON serializable
```

The report runs inside `VllmConfig.with_hf_config`, which every speculative setup takes when it registers its draft model, so GLM-5.3-Flash with its MTP head cannot start on current `main` (4e5357b59). Observed on 4x V100 with the EXL3 checkpoint through #1102 + #1125 + #1159; the failing frame is `vllm/sm70_profiles/acceleration.py:30` under `init_vllm_registered_model` for `Glm5NextMTPModel`.

## Change

`vllm/sm70_profiles/acceleration.py`: both `json.dumps(asdict(...))` calls get a `default=` hook that encodes sets as sorted lists, tuples as lists, and anything else unknown through `repr`, instead of failing. No behaviour change for policies without set-valued fields.

## Not a duplicate

No open or closed PR touches the acceleration report's serialization (searched "frozenset", "linear_policy_report", "acceleration report").

## Test Plan

- `tests/sm70_profiles/test_sm70_acceleration_report.py` (new): a dataclass policy tree with `frozenset`, `None` and tuple fields produces a plain-JSON report with sorted lists.
- E2E: GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 (TP4, MTP k=3, FP8 KV, CUDA graphs) on `main` + #1125 + #1159 + #1102 + this fix, which fails at engine init without it.
- ruff on the changed files.

## Test Result

- Unit test: 1 passed (on a full SM70 build of `main` 4e5357b59 + #1125 + #1159 + #1102 + this commit).
- E2E: with this fix the stack reaches model load and (on `main` ec60883ad, before the second init-time regression described in the comment below) serves GLM-5.3-Flash at 85.7 tok/s decode with the model card's command; on `main` 4e5357b59 it then hits the Flash-V100 binding error reported in the comment.
- ruff 0.14.0 format and check clean.

Gates before review:

- [x] Test against an independent expectation (hand-built policy tree), failing without the change
- [x] ruff on the changed files
- [x] Full wheel build (CMake path) and the test on it
- [x] E2E (see above)

nodes.body:
With this fix applied, the same stack (`main` 4e5357b59 + #1125 + #1159 + #1102) fails later in the same init path, which looks like a second regression from the 10 Oct provider-lifecycle series (first-parent merge d4ce51399, #1148, "Rebind runtime owners after worker transfer" and the commits that followed):

```
vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/selector.py:180 _auto_select_mla_prefill_backend
vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flash_attn.py:67 is_available
vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_v100/dense_prefill.py:922 flash_v100_dense_prefill_lse_available
vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_v100/ops.py:375 get_flash_dense_forward
vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_v100/runtime.py:38 bind_attention_operation
RuntimeError: Flash-V100 resources must be bound before execution
```

The MLA prefill selector probes `FlashAttnPrefillBackend.is_available()` while the model is being built, and on SM70 that probe now binds Flash-V100 runtime resources, which `forward_context.activate_runtime_resources` only provides at execution time. The selector catches `ImportError` only, so the `RuntimeError` aborts worker init. `main` at ec60883ad (the parent of that merge) does not have the check and the stack starts and runs there; I have not changed anything in that path and am reporting it here rather than guessing at the intended binding order.
